title: A Notion page references a GitHub issue or PR number that doesn't exist
author: zashiki-warashi
description: The eleventh leg of the dangling-reference family (dangling-issue-reference watches commit messages, mention-dangling-reference watches X mentions, release-note-dangling-reference watches release notes, issue-body-dangling-reference watches issue/PR opening bodies, milestone-body-dangling-reference watches milestone descriptions, own-tweet-dangling-reference watches the town's own tweets, review-comment-dangling-reference watches a PR's own inline review comments, issue-comment-dangling-reference watches the ordinary issue/PR timeline, linear-comment-dangling-reference watches a comment left on Linear, slack-message-dangling-reference watches a Slack channel message), and the first recipe to read a Notion page at all. Extracts every same-repo #N reference (seam_engine.references.referenced_numbers, the one shared grammar ten sibling dangling-reference recipes already import) from a Notion page's own title+body text and checks it against both the live issue list AND the live PR list -- GitHub shares one number sequence between the two, so a reference must be checked against both or it would misfire on a perfectly good reference to a merged PR. This is also the first recipe to ask the oath for a Notion READ scope: SCOPES.md had only ever named Notion for CreatePage (draftback.py's one authorized write); SearchPages is the read-side analog of slack's SearchChannelMessages and linear's SearchIssueComments, added to consent.REQUIRED_SCOPES, SCOPES.md's oath table, and point-fencepost.md's issue template in this same commit. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, same WIP shape every other non-GitHub/X toolkit in this engine already carries: the-hand's live gateway exposes zero Notion-read tools today.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the page's own last_edited_at, holding issue-comment-dangling-reference's, linear-comment-dangling-reference's, and slack-message-dangling-reference's identical 0.85/0.55 edit-grace-window bar exactly (24 hours) -- a Notion page, like an ordinary GitHub issue comment, a Linear comment, or a Slack message and unlike an immutable X mention, is a text surface its author can still edit at any time, so a reference caught within the grace window scores the lower bar (0.55) rather than the higher one (0.85) a stale, unedited reference earns. A reference matching a real issue or PR (either tracker, GitHub's shared number sequence) is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the reference was simply good. A page with no #N reference at all produces no candidate whatsoever, not even an excluded one -- it never claims anything about a second record, so there is no seam to weigh. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades whoever wrote the page -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
